From: Sarah Lamont <sarah.lamont@edgeify.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live feed gap + websocket timeouts — happening since 08:50 PT

Jordan —

We started seeing large gaps in streaming responses from Redwood at ~08:50 PT this morning. Clients report repeated WebSocket timeouts and missing token chunks (partial finalization). Error rate on our side spiked from ~0.3% to 6% and median latency increased from 120ms to ~1.8s for streaming calls. This is affecting our realtime personalization demos across multiple regions.

Attached are a short sampled client trace and server-side logs showing repeated "WS: read timeout" events and chunk sequence gaps.

We need an immediate triage and a timeline to resolution — our execs are pressing for an update. Can you confirm whether this is a localized routing issue or something platform-wide?

Attaching: diag-trace-20271102.zip (contains client trace and sequence logs)

Thanks,
Sarah Lamont
Head of Platform Reliability
Edgeify Inc

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:20 AM jordan_blake@redwood.com wrote:
> Forwarding — from Edgeify (large customer, near-term expansion). They report a sudden spike...

Checked infra metrics for us-west-2: no host restarts, but we see a correlated increase in kernel-level syscall queue length on the proxy fleet serving their tenant and a 4x spike in small-payload concurrent requests between 08:48–08:58. TCP keepalive retransmits also rose.

Preliminary hypothesis: a transient upstream congestion event (CDN at Edgeify's side or intermediate network) caused bursty reconnects which overloaded the proxy connection pool, leading to per-connection stalls and chunk assembly timeouts. Runtime telemetry shows queuing at the proxy layer rather than model runtime stalls.

Actionables (in progress):
- Increasing proxy connection pool and backpressure timers for the affected route (rolling config now).
- Gathering full pcap snippets and the proxy logs around the spike window.
- Kicking off a controlled throttle to flatten retries for that route if we keep seeing >2x baseline retries.

I'll post logs to the Zoom channel.

— Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:45 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Preliminary hypothesis: a transient upstream congestion event...

Quick runtime check: no new kernel selection commits in the last 48h that match this behavior. However, we do see an edge-level burst where the continuous-batching boundary timer expired repeatedly causing partial payload flushes; combined with proxy-level replays this could explain out-of-order chunk frames and token loss on client assembly.

Mitigations applied (10:00–10:03):
- Raised batching window from 5ms -> 12ms for the affected route to allow more stable chunk coalescing.
- Extended WS keepalive threshold temporarily from 30s -> 60s for the tenant.

Monitoring now (watching chunk success rate and error rate). If the error rate doesn't drop below 1% in the next 20 minutes, I'll flip on the fallback policy to route to the larger-memory model variant that tolerates longer assembly windows.

— Hannah
Runtime Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lamont <sarah.lamont@edgeify.com>, ops@edgeify.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Live feed gap + websocket timeouts — happening since 08:50 PT

Sarah / Edgeify team —

Thanks for raising this and for the traces. Quick update and what we’ve done so far:

1) What happened (short): between ~08:48–08:58 PT a burst of client reconnects and rapid small-payload requests caused proxy connection pools to hit a queuing threshold. That queueing combined with aggressive batching boundaries produced partial chunk flushes and apparent token gaps on the client.

2) Immediate mitigations (completed):
- Increased proxy connection pool size and smoothed backpressure timers for your route (rolled at 09:05).
- Adjusted continuous-batching window and extended keepalive thresholds (rolled at 10:03).
- Enabled temporary routing fallback to a model variant with higher tolerance for chunk assembly (if we detect >1% error rate for 10m).

3) Current status (12:30 PT): error rate back down to ~0.9%, median streaming latency at ~160ms. We continue to monitor.

4) Next steps / plan:
- Karthik to provide full proxy logs + pcap snippet (JIRA INFRA-1427) for root cause analysis by EOD.
- We will run a replay of the burst at 2pm PT in a mirrored test environment to stress the proxy pool and validate permanent tuning changes.
- We'll propose a longer-term fix: smarter tokenized chunk reassembly retry logic at the proxy layer + adaptive batching based on small-payload burst detection.

We are treating this as a Sev2 for impact (customer-facing SLO risk). I'll follow up with a concise incident summary and timeline for your execs within 3 hours. Apologies again for the disruption — we know how visible this was for your demos.

If you need immediate visibility, I'm on the support Zoom now: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210 (also looping in Karthik & Hannah).

Best,
Jordan Blake
